# The Rosetta Project

> A digital archive and preservation initiative documenting endangered and minority languages worldwide through microfilm technology, parallel speech corpora, and crowdsourced linguistic contributions.

The Rosetta Project preserves human linguistic diversity through innovative long-term storage methods and collaborative language documentation. Founded with support from The Long Now Foundation, it combines cutting-edge microetching technology with open-access linguistic resources to ensure languages are not lost to future generations.

## Core Mission & Technology

- [Building an Archive of ALL Documented Human Languages](https://rosettaproject.org): Homepage for The Rosetta Project, an archive of documented human languages.
- [About - The Rosetta Project](https://rosettaproject.org/about): Overview of The Rosetta Project's mission and the Rosetta Disk technology.
- [Concept - The Rosetta Project](https://rosettaproject.org/disk/concept): Explains the Rosetta Disk concept and microetching technology for long-term preservation.
- [Rosetta Wearable Disk - The Rosetta Project](https://rosettaproject.org/wearable): Rosetta Wearable Disk product featuring microfilm technology for portable archiving.

## Language Documentation Projects

- [300 Languages: A Parallel Speech Corpus Project - The Rosetta Project](https://rosettaproject.org/projects/300-languages): The 300 Languages Project for parallel speech corpus and multilingual documentation.
- [About the 300 Languages Project - The Rosetta Project](http://rosettaproject.org/projects/300-languages/about): Documentation about the 300 Languages Project methodology and linguistic research.
- [Make a New Translation - The Rosetta Project](http://rosettaproject.org/projects/300-languages/new-translation): How-to guide for creating new translations using Swadesh lists and standards.
- [Submitting a Translation - The Rosetta Project](http://rosettaproject.org/projects/300-languages/submit-translation): Guide for submitting translations using ISO 639-3 standards and naming conventions.

## Community Contribution & Recording

- [Make a New Recording - The Rosetta Project](http://rosettaproject.org/projects/300-languages/new-recording): Guide for recording new audio contributions with microphone setup and file formats.
- [Record-a-thon: Guidelines for Speakers - The Rosetta Project](http://rosettaproject.org/record-a-thon/guidelines-speakers): Guidelines for native speakers participating in record-a-thon events.
- [Upload a File - The Rosetta Project](http://rosettaproject.org/record-a-thon/upload/posttest): Instructions for uploading language recordings to the record-a-thon platform.

## Get Involved & Support
